messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Prod: elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed for private-vpc endpoints (vpc-prod-022). Metric: HTTP 5xx rate spiking from 0.2% -> 8% in the last 3m. Root: connection timeouts/gateway errors from pods in private subnets. Auto-page: @sam (oncall), @maria (neteng), @alex (sre)

sam (oncall): on it. seeing a lot of 502/504 from gateway LB logs. Marking P1. Triage plan: 1) confirm scope/customers 2) check NAT/Route/Peering 3) mitigate (scale NAT / failover) 4) notify customers.

alex (sre): I pulled the LB logs: majority of requests to /v1/generate are returning 502 with "upstream connection timed out". Traces show ECONNRESET at gateway to private backends.

jordan (eng): can we confirm it's only the private deployment (VPC) and not hosted? telemetry shows hosted endpoints OK.

maria (neteng): quick health checks: VPC peering status green, but NAT gateway metrics look saturated. ConnTrackCount ~ 65000 (limit ~65536) on nat-igw-1 in az-a. Packet drops and timeouts align with the spike. Possible conntrack exhaustion causing new connections to be dropped -> gateway timeouts.

sam (oncall): that fits. any recent config changes to egress security groups or route tables?

maria (neteng): no recent SG changes in last 24h. route tables unchanged. Traffic pattern shows burst from model-serving pods (long-lived connections + many ephemeral ones). We have high bursts after a rollout that increased concurrency per pod.

alex (sre): mitigation options: 1) increase NAT capacity (create additional NAT gateway in another AZ and update route table to use a NAT gateway with higher throughput) 2) offload some traffic via a public egress path for critical customers (temporary) 3) tune conntrack on NAT instances (if using NAT instances) or request provider increase if managed NAT.

sam (oncall): quick wins first: - create second NAT in az-b, add to route table for private subnets (balance across AZs). - temporarily lower concurrency limits on model-serving group for private deployment to reduce new connections.

jordan (eng): rolling a concurrency cap now to 8 per worker for private cluster. patch: `kubectl -n model set env ds/model-serving CONCURRENCY=8` (will rollout in 60s).

maria (neteng): creating NAT in az-b now (aws cli):
```
aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-0b --allocation-id eipalloc-12345
aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-prod-022
```
Once created, I'll update route table for the private subnets to point to a route-target set that uses a simple latency-based route to pick between nat-1 and nat-2.

cloud-support-bot: NAT gateway create request submitted. NAT id: nat-08a3xxxx. Provisioning ETA ~ 45s.

alex (sre): meanwhile I'm enabling a temporary fallback route for the most critical customers to go via hosted fallback (edge-hosted) — config change in router: `route-match /v1/generate customer in {alpha,beta} -> edge-hosted-pool`. This will reduce load on private backends by ~30%.

sam (oncall): support thread prep: @taylor please draft the customer-facing note for impacted customers with status + mitigation steps and SLO impact. Keep it short: outage vs degraded, ETA for fix ~ 20-40m.

taylor (support): drafting now. Initial customer impact: API error rate up to 12% for private deployments, affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Impacted customers identified: cust-alpha (10% of traffic), cust-gamma (5%), misc self-hosted clients (rest). Will publish an incident banner on status page referencing our backend issue and mitigation (partial failover).

maria (neteng): NAT status: healthy. Updated route tables for subnets private-subnet-{a,b,c} to use a new route table association that allows per-AZ NAT use. ConnTrackCount on nat-08a3xxxx now 12000 after cutover; overall conntrack drop events falling.

sam (oncall): can we see error rates?

incident-bot: Metrics snapshot: 5xx rate now 3.1% (was 8.0), p50 latency unchanged, p95 improved slightly. Request volume same.

alex (sre): concurrency cap rollout completed. pods are healthy. 502s trending down. I'll keep rollback path ready if we see other regressions.

jordan (eng): confirm: no SG changes needed, all good. Also recommending we add a connection pooler / keepalive optimization for egress to reduce ephemeral connections. Filing an RFC for early next sprint.

maria (neteng): quick note: we observed CT (conntrack) entries with TIME_WAIT explosion caused by many short-lived outbound connections. Long-term mitigations: 1) NAT autoscale policy 2) conntrack tuning or managed provider upgrade 3) egress proxy to reuse connections.

sam (oncall): timeline for postmortem: start doc, include root cause (conntrack exhaustion on NAT), mitigation steps taken, customers impacted, action items. I'll own the incident doc creation.

cloud-support-bot: Provider support ticket opened: Case #CS-78912. They acknowledged NAT scaling scenario and suggested increasing NAT TGW capacity and verifying conntrack limits for peak throughput.

taylor (support): sent status update to customers and posted banner. Several customers acknowledged and asked for ETA — forwarding to eng.

alex (sre): monitoring: keep an eye on 5xx and NAT conntrack metrics. Alerting adjusted: new alert when NAT conntrack > 55k or when 5xx>2% sustained for 5m.

sam (oncall): handing this to night oncall @lee at 03:00 UTC. Summary: transient conntrack exhaustion on managed NAT caused gateway timeouts for private VPC; we provisioned additional NAT and updated route tables, rolled back concurrency increases that caused the burst, and enabled temporary hosted fallback for critical customers. 5xx reduced from 8% -> 0.8% by last check. Postmortem doc link: (I'll create).

maria (neteng): adding action items to network backlog: - implement NAT autoscale trigger - evaluate managed NAT limits across regions - build an egress proxy/connection pooler - add chaos test for conntrack exhaustion.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. If errors reappear escalate to P1. :white_check_mark:

sam (oncall): closing the immediate P1. Leaving the doc open and monitoring for 2 more hours. Thanks all for quick response.
